how: A member proposed a visible FIRST mark that others selected, mapped, and volunteered to help build.
Repeated invitations recruited helpers to build, repair, and defend the logo at specified pixels.
A direct volunteering reply accepts the proposal briefly, while another promise qualifies participation by current availability.
Members selected the logo, proposed lettering, added the related robotics community, and requested aligned letters.
Reports of starting, improving, completing letters, and ongoing construction describe building as well as maintenance.
A requested grid was made smaller and participants asked that its image and anchor coordinates be published.
Members used bots and spare accounts while disputing whether scripting was scummy, unprofessional, necessary, or ineffective.
Shared automation requires replacing or disabling obsolete targets because old scripts can obstruct progress.
When automation fails, participants can continue manual repair alongside troubleshooting rather than abandon placement.

statement: Routing helpers between public threads and chat-held plans
how: Explicit chat referrals explain how helpers find plans and diplomacy beyond templates and public state reports.
Public referrals identify unseen chat planning but cannot establish whether leaders, votes, sanctions, or task divisions were decided there.
Members repaired altered lettering, watched for vandalism, prioritized the main logo, and called for continuing maintenance.
Participants corrected blame and distinguished allied collectives from rogue placers without settling the final cause of loss.
Attribution must preserve which mark a report concerns because the colour-infighting account explicitly describes the AMD logo.
Neighbours invoked agreements, disputed an apparent breach, and described a peaceful alliance that respected property.
Negotiation may begin during initial space selection before a completed mark needs defending.
Agreement compliance depends on participants learning the agreement, so a reminder can expose ignorance rather than rejection of authority.
Participants spared harmless neighbouring work and answered a damage complaint with apologies.
An apology evidences acknowledgement of damage but does not establish restoration of the overwritten artwork.
A visitor offered pixels and directed diplomacy to chat, while another request was refused without a surviving explanation of its contents.
Returning contested space was accompanied by an offer to help the other team.
An alliance invitation and requests for joint lettering support cooperation between related robotics communities.
The member carrying an alliance invitation speaks for the inviting robotics community in that encounter.
A reported permission to draw into a neighbouring flag does not establish continuing host authority over guest work.
Participants reported abandoning a contested location and later moving the logo down with neighbouring help.
Distinguish relocation for preventive accommodation from post-erasure rebuilding when speakers explain movement as avoiding conflict.
Relocation requires changing the automation target as well as announcing the new coordinates.
A participant judged the neighbouring faction potentially stronger and proposed less resisted space.
Ignorance of an agreement and distinctions between allies and rogues do not show anyone disputing who may bind the room.
A participant evaluated scripts through Gracious Professionalism, bringing a community norm into the choice of means.
Retrospective team-number and invasion disputes do not establish a quarrel carried into the canvas from beforehand.
Historical Poland jokes occur retrospectively and do not establish inherited rivalry naming a target in an initiating attack turn.
A duplicate-post referral documents coordination but no coded passage establishes canvas-specific host moderation or posting restrictions.
Feeling bamboozled after the damaged ending does not establish that the host framed its original canvas call as a prank.
Participants repeatedly celebrated progress and completion, including claiming that the room had made its mark.

statement: Drawing a canvas viewer into the room
how: A viewer explicitly discovered the subreddit through its canvas logo, showing a return of visibility beyond celebrating the mark.
Members marked shutdown and answered impossible repair calls with recognition that placement had stopped.
Participants preserved preferred memories and openly edited a final image into what the logo was supposed to look like.
Mourning acknowledged both pride in the intended final logo and fragments remaining after the loss.
Corrections of blame contest the event account by distinguishing rogues from allied members and naming another alleged overbuilder.
An acknowledged counterfactual edit and duplicate-post objection do not establish a contest over an authoritative shared cleanup.
Disappointment prompted successor-canvas proposals, a question about location, and concrete starting coordinates.
A successor proposal and coordinate establish an attempt to continue but leave actual completion and persistence unresolved.
Disappointment with the damaged outcome explicitly supplies a reason to try the logo again elsewhere.
Participants proposed opposing a neighbouring flag and taking space, without proving a coordinated room-wide raid.
Post-close blame and retrospective invasion jokes continued the contest in talk while responsibility remained disputed.
Retrospective accusations remain attributed claims rather than proof of which group initiated destruction.
A starter's proposal received an explicit volunteering reply, giving local support to a proposal gathering willing hands.
Invitations precede building reports but no cited passage identifies which call caused particular builders to join.
The proposal receives a bare volunteering answer, supporting the acceptance pattern without measuring silent placement responses.
A request for a logo grid receives a reply supplying and shrinking that grid.
Building and maintenance can overlap because a repair report is answered by clarification that construction is still underway.
Defensive scripting is justified as necessary by participants, while manual fallback and expansion uses prevent inferring exclusive necessity or demonstrated success.
The record shows early treaty proposals and later upkeep beside agreements but does not establish upkeep causing the negotiation.
An explicit treaty refusal is followed by an explanation that the alliance is peaceful and respects property.
Offers of help are visible but the coded passages do not establish shortage-driven requests causing their arrival.
Treaty reports and help coexist without a preserved bargain demonstrating that border negotiation generated reciprocal assistance.
The alliance invitation occurs amid upkeep but does not explicitly attribute coalition formation to shared attack pressure.
A strength warning and a later accommodation move do not establish that insufficient hands caused the room to stop fighting and relocate.
An achievement explanation specifies making the logo and subreddit lettering within a completion thread.
Celebration and later preservation are visible but no cited passage makes celebration the cause of recording.
Successor calls explicitly answer disappointment but do not identify a preserved record as the cause of continuing elsewhere.
Recruitment precedes expansion proposals without evidence that mobilization itself caused participants to attack.
A proposal to oppose the neighbouring flag receives a reasoned warning about superior numbers and an alternative with less resistance.
A treaty is invoked to refuse destruction but the coded record lacks the full initiating attack call needed to establish that transition.
Retrospective invasion claims and blame connect the subject matter but do not independently establish the initiating attack and resulting talk.
Calls and a duplicate-post referral provide no coded evidence that a canvas flood produced host posting restrictions.
Agreement reminders receive an explanation of ignorance rather than a dispute over representative authority.
